Create source-grounded retrieval evaluation questions. Return JSON {"items":[...]}.
For EACH supplied source return {"id":same id,"en":English patient question,"zh":Chinese patient question,
"evidence_id":the exact id string of ONE supplied evidence_options entry supporting BOTH questions}.
Ask one concrete question about a supported detail (cause, symptom, prevention, evaluation, management).
The two questions express the SAME information need, not two facts. Use ordinary patient language.
Include enough topic context to identify the condition but do not copy a source sentence into the question.
Select an evidence option and ask about a concrete detail stated in that option. Do not ask for a personalized dose or individual diagnosis. Do not invent content. No answers in questions.
These are synthetic topic-source retrieval labels, not a clinician-authored benchmark.

[{"id": "MLP-600", "title": "Bipolar Disorder", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Bipolar disorder is a mood disorder that can cause intense mood swings: Sometimes you may feel extremely \"up,\" elated, irritable, or energized."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Other times you may feel \"down,\" sad, indifferent, or hopeless."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "You may have both manic and depressive symptoms together."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Along with mood swings, bipolar disorder causes changes in behavior, energy levels, and activity levels."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Bipolar disorder used to be called other names, including manic depression and manic-depressive disorder."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "There are three main types of bipolar disorder: Bipolar I disorder involves manic episodes that last at least 7 days or manic symptoms so severe that you need immediate hospital care."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "This type of bipolar disorder can also involve mixed episodes."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Bipolar II disorder involves depressive episodes."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "But instead of full-blown manic episodes, there are episodes of hypomania."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Hypomania is a less severe version of mania."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Cyclothymic disorder , or cyclothymia, also involves hypomanic and depressive symptoms."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "But they are not as intense or as long-lasting as hypomanic or depressive episodes."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "The symptoms usually last for at least two years in adults and for one year in children and teenagers."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "With any of these types, having four or more episodes of mania or depression in a year is called \"rapid cycling.\" What causes bipolar disorder?"}, {"id": "S014", "text": "The exact cause of bipolar disorder is unknown."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "Several factors likely play a role in the disorder."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "They include genetics , brain structure and function, and your environment."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "You are at higher risk for bipolar disorder if you have a close relative who has it."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "Going through trauma or stressful life events may raise this risk even more."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "What are the symptoms of bipolar disorder?"}, {"id": "S020", "text": "The symptoms of bipolar disorder can vary."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "But they involve mood swings known as mood episodes: The symptoms of a manic episode can include: Feeling very up, high, or elated Feeling jumpy or wired, more active than usual Having a very short temper or seeming extremely irritable Having racing thoughts and talking very fast Needing less sleep Feeling like you are unusually important, talented, or powerful Do risky things that show poor judgment, such as eating and drinking too much, spending or giving away a lot of money, or having reckless sex The symptoms of a depressive episode can include: Feeling very sad, hopeless, or worthless Feeling lonely or isolating yourself from others Talking very slowly, feeling like you have nothing to say, or forgetting a lot Having little energy Sleeping too much Eating too much or too little Lack of interest in your usual activities and being unable to do even simple things Thinking about death or suicide The symptoms of a mixed episode include both manic and depressive symptoms together."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "For example, you may feel very sad, empty, or hopeless, while at the same time feeling extremely energized."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "Some people with bipolar disorder may have milder symptoms."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "For example, you may have hypomania instead of mania."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "With hypomania, you may feel very good and find that you can get a lot done."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "You may not feel like anything is wrong."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "But your family and friends may notice your mood swings and changes in activity levels."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "They may realize that your behavior is unusual for you."}, {"id": "S029", "text": "After the hypomania, you might have severe depression."}, {"id": "S030", "text": "Your mood episodes may last a week or two or sometimes longer."}, {"id": "S031", "text": "During an episode, symptoms usually occur every day for most of the day."}, {"id": "S032", "text": "To diagnose bipolar disorder, your health care provider may use many tools: A physical exam A medical history, which will include asking about your symptoms, lifetime history, experiences, and family history Medical tests to rule out other conditions A mental health evaluation."}, {"id": "S033", "text": "Your provider may do the evaluation or may refer you to a mental health specialist to get one."}, {"id": "S034", "text": "What are the treatments for bipolar disorder?"}, {"id": "S035", "text": "Treatment can help many people, including those with the most severe forms of bipolar disorder."}, {"id": "S036", "text": "The main treatments for bipolar disorder include medicines, psychotherapy, or both: Medicines can help control the symptoms of bipolar disorder."}, {"id": "S037", "text": "You may need to try several different medicines to find which one works best for you."}, {"id": "S038", "text": "Some people need to take more than one medicine."}, {"id": "S039", "text": "It's important to take your medicine consistently."}, {"id": "S040", "text": "Don't stop taking it without first talking with your provider."}, {"id": "S041", "text": "Contact your provider if you have any concerns about side effects from the medicines."}, {"id": "S042", "text": "Psychotherapy (talk therapy) can help you recognize and change troubling emotions, thoughts, and behaviors."}, {"id": "S043", "text": "It can give you and your family support, education, skills, and coping strategies."}, {"id": "S044", "text": "There are several different types of psychotherapy that may help with bipolar disorder."}, {"id": "S045", "text": "Other treatment options include: Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT), a brain stimulation procedure that can help relieve symptoms."}, {"id": "S046", "text": "It uses a mild electric current and is done while you are under general anesthesia."}, {"id": "S047", "text": "ECT is most often used for severe bipolar disorder that is not getting better with other treatments."}, {"id": "S048", "text": "It may also be used when someone needs a treatment that will work more quickly than medicines."}, {"id": "S049", "text": "This might be when a person has a high risk of suicide or is catatonic (unresponsive)."}, {"id": "S050", "text": "Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS), a brain stimulation procedure that uses magnetic waves to relieve depression."}, {"id": "S051", "text": "It is not as powerful as ECT, but with rTMS, you don't need general anesthesia."}, {"id": "S052", "text": "It also has a low risk of negative effects on your memory and thinking."}, {"id": "S053", "text": "Light therapy has been shown to be effective for seasonal affective disorder (SAD)."}, {"id": "S054", "text": "Many people with bipolar disorder also find that their depression gets worse during certain seasons, usually in the fall and winter."}, {"id": "S055", "text": "Light therapy may help with their symptoms."}, {"id": "S056", "text": "Healthy lifestyle changes, such as getting regular exercise, having a consistent sleep schedule, and keeping a mood journal, can also help with your symptoms."}, {"id": "S057", "text": "But long-term, ongoing treatment can help manage your symptoms and enable you to live a healthy, successful life."}, {"id": "S058", "text": "NIH: National Institute of Mental Health"}]}, {"id": "MLP-237", "title": "Eating Disorders", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Eating disorders are serious mental health disorders."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "They involve severe problems with your thoughts about food and your eating behaviors."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "You may eat much less or much more than you need."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Eating disorders are medical conditions; they are not a lifestyle choice."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "They affect your body's ability to get proper nutrition."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "This can lead to health issues, such as heart and kidney problems, or sometimes even death."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Common types of eating disorders include: Binge-eating , which is out-of-control eating."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "People with binge-eating disorder keep eating even after they are full."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "They often eat until they feel very uncomfortable."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Afterward, they usually have feelings of guilt, shame, and distress."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Eating too much too often can lead to weight gain and obesity ."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "Binge-eating disorder is the most common eating disorder in the U.S."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "People with bulimia nervosa also have periods of binge-eating."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "But afterwards, they purge, by making themselves throw up or using laxatives."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "People with bulimia nervosa may be slightly underweight, normal weight, or overweight."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "People with anorexia nervosa avoid food, severely restrict food, or eat very small quantities of only certain foods."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "They may see themselves as overweight, even when they are dangerously underweight."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "Anorexia nervosa is the least common of the three eating disorders, but it is often the most serious."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "It has the highest death rate of any mental disorder."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "The exact cause of eating disorders is unknown."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "Researchers believe that eating disorders are caused by a complex interaction of factors."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "These include genetic, biological, behavioral, psychological, and social factors."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "Anyone can develop an eating disorder, but they are more common in women."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "Eating disorders frequently appear during the teen years or young adulthood."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "But people can also develop them during childhood or later in life."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "What are the symptoms of eating disorders?"}, {"id": "S026", "text": "The symptoms of eating disorders vary, depending on the disorder: The symptoms of binge-eating include: Eating unusually large amounts of food in a specific amount of time, such as a 2-hour period Eating even when you're full or not hungry Eating fast during binge episodes Eating until you're uncomfortably full Eating alone or in secret to avoid embarrassment Feeling distressed, ashamed, or guilty about your eating Frequently dieting, possibly without weight loss The symptoms of bulimia nervosa include the same symptoms as binge-eating, plus trying to get rid of the food or weight after binging by: Purging, making yourself throw up or using laxatives or enemas to speed up the movement of food through your body Doing intensive and excessive exercise Fasting Over time, bulimia nervosa can cause health problems such as: Chronically inflamed and sore throat Swollen salivary glands in the neck and jaw area Worn tooth enamel and increasingly sensitive and decaying teeth ."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "This is caused by the exposure to stomach acid every time you throw up."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "GERD (acid reflux) and other gastrointestinal problems Severe dehydration from purging Electrolyte imbalance , which could be too low or too high levels of sodium, calcium, potassium and other minerals."}, {"id": "S029", "text": "This can lead to a stroke or heart attack ."}, {"id": "S030", "text": "The symptoms of anorexia nervosa include: Eating very little, to the point of starving yourself Intensive and excessive exercise Extreme thinness Intense fear of gaining weight Distorted body image - seeing yourself as overweight even when you are severely underweight Over time, anorexia nervosa can cause health problems such as: Thinning of the bones (osteopenia or osteoporosis ) Mild anemia Muscle wasting and weakness Thin, brittle hair and nails Dry, blotchy, or yellowish skin Growth of fine hair all over the body Severe constipation Low blood pressure Slowed breathing and pulse Feeling cold all the time because of a drop in internal body temperature Feeling faint, dizzy , or weak Feeling tired all the time Infertility Damage to the structure and function of the heart Brain damage Multiorgan failure Anorexia nervosa can be fatal."}, {"id": "S031", "text": "Some people with this disorder die of complications from starvation, and others die of suicide ."}, {"id": "S032", "text": "Some people with eating disorders may also have other mental disorders (such as depression or anxiety ) or problems with substance use ."}, {"id": "S033", "text": "Because eating disorders can be so serious, it is important to seek help if you or a loved one thinks that you might have a problem."}, {"id": "S034", "text": "Your health care provider may use many tools to make a diagnosis: A medical history, which includes asking about your symptoms."}, {"id": "S035", "text": "It is important to be honest about your eating and exercise behaviors so your provider can help you."}, {"id": "S036", "text": "A physical exam Blood or urine tests to rule out other possible causes of your symptoms Other tests to see whether you have any other health problems caused by the eating disorder."}, {"id": "S037", "text": "These can include kidney function tests and an electrocardiogram (EKG or ECG)."}, {"id": "S038", "text": "What are the treatments for eating disorders?"}, {"id": "S039", "text": "Treatment plans for eating disorders are tailored to individual needs."}, {"id": "S040", "text": "You will likely have a team of providers helping you, including doctors, nutritionists, nurses, and therapists."}, {"id": "S041", "text": "The treatments may include: Individual, group, and/or family psychotherapy."}, {"id": "S042", "text": "Individual therapy may include cognitive behavioral approaches, which help you to identify and change negative and unhelpful thoughts."}, {"id": "S043", "text": "It also helps you build coping skills and change behavioral patterns."}, {"id": "S044", "text": "Medical care and monitoring, including care for the complications that eating disorders can cause Nutrition counseling."}, {"id": "S045", "text": "Doctors, nurses, and counselors will help you eat healthy to reach and maintain a healthy weight."}, {"id": "S046", "text": "Medicines, such as antidepressants , antipsychotics, or mood stabilizers, may help treat some eating disorders."}, {"id": "S047", "text": "The medicines can also help with the depression and anxiety symptoms that often go along with eating disorders."}, {"id": "S048", "text": "Some people with serious eating disorders may need to be in a hospital or in a residential treatment program."}, {"id": "S049", "text": "Residential treatment programs combine housing and treatment services."}, {"id": "S050", "text": "NIH: National Institute of Mental Health"}]}, {"id": "MLP-1339", "title": "Diabetes Type 1", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Diabetes means your blood glucose , also called blood sugar, is too high."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "With type 1 diabetes, your body makes little or no insulin."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Insulin is a hormone from your pancreas that helps glucose move from your body into your cells, where it is used for energy."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Your body can make glucose, but it also comes from the food you eat."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Without insulin, too much glucose stays in your blood."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Over time, high blood glucose can lead to serious problems with your heart , eyes , kidneys , nerves , gums, and teeth."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "If your blood glucose gets very high, you can develop diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA)."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "It happens when your body doesn't have enough insulin to allow glucose into your cells."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Instead, your liver breaks down fat for energy, which produces ketones."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "When ketones build up too quickly, they can reach dangerous levels."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Type 1 diabetes is an autoimmune disease ."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "Your immune system mistakenly attacks the cells in your pancreas that make insulin."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "Researchers don't yet know exactly why this happens."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "Genes and environmental factors may play a role in triggering the disease."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "Who is more likely to develop type 1 diabetes?"}, {"id": "S015", "text": "Type 1 diabetes often begins in children and young adults, but it can appear at any age."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "Having a parent or sibling with type 1 diabetes may increase your chance of developing it."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "What are the symptoms of type 1 diabetes?"}, {"id": "S018", "text": "Symptoms often start quickly, especially in children."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "In adults, they may develop more slowly."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "Symptoms may include: Feeling very thirsty Feeling very hungry Urinating (peeing) more often, including at night Having fatigue Having blurry vision Losing feeling in your feet, or having tingling in your feet or hands Having sores that don't heal Losing weight without trying How is type 1 diabetes diagnosed?"}, {"id": "S021", "text": "Blood tests that measure your blood glucose level can show whether it is higher than normal for you."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "What are the treatments for type 1 diabetes?"}, {"id": "S023", "text": "Type 1 diabetes is a chronic (long-term) condition."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "You will need daily insulin, either through injections or an insulin pump."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "Some people also take another diabetes medicine that works with insulin."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "Ask your health care provider about the best way to check your blood glucose level and how often you should check it."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "But you may be able to prevent or delay health problems related to diabetes by: Managing your blood glucose level with finger prick tests or a continuous glucose monitor (CGM) Making healthy food choices Getting regular exercise A blood test called the A1C can show how well you are managing your diabetes over time."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "NIH: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases"}]}, {"id": "MLP-292", "title": "Hysterectomy", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "A hysterectomy is surgery to remove the uterus (womb)."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "The uterus is the place where a fetus grows during pregnancy."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "A hysterectomy treats problems like heavy bleeding, pain, or cancer in the uterus."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "After a hysterectomy, you no longer have menstrual periods and can't become pregnant."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Sometimes the surgery also removes the ovaries and fallopian tubes."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "If you have both ovaries taken out, menopause symptoms will usually begin."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "What conditions does a hysterectomy treat?"}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Your health care provider may suggest other treatment options first."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "These might include medicine, hormone therapy, or procedures to remove fibroids or stop heavy bleeding."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Sometimes these won't help, or surgery might be the only option, depending on the condition that needs to be treated."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Your provider might recommend a hysterectomy if you have: Fibroids , if you are near or past menopause, have large fibroids or very heavy bleeding."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "Endometriosis , that hasn't been cured by medicine or surgery."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "Uterine prolapse , which can happen after several vaginal births, menopause, or because of obesity."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "It is when the uterus drops into the vagina."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "Cancer , of the uterus , cervix , ovaries , or endometrium (the lining of the uterus)."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "Vaginal bleeding , that is heavy or unusual and persists despite treatment."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "Chronic pelvic pain , which starts in the uterus."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "A hysterectomy is a last resort since it doesn't fix some pelvic pain."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "Adenomyosis , is a thickening of the walls of the uterus."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "A hysterectomy is only considered if pain is severe and no other treatments have worked."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "What are the different types of hysterectomies?"}, {"id": "S021", "text": "Your provider will discuss the type of hysterectomy you need, depending on your condition."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "The different types of surgeries include: A total hysterectomy is the most common type and involves the removal of all the uterus, including the cervix."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "The ovaries and fallopian tubes may or may not be removed."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "A partial (subtotal or supracervical) hysterectomy removes just the upper part of the uterus."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "The cervix is left in place, and your ovaries may or may not be removed A radical hysterectomy removes all the uterus, cervix, and tissue on both sides of the cervix and the upper part of the vagina."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "This is most often used to treat certain types of cancer, such as cervical cancer."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "The fallopian tubes and ovaries may or may not be removed."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "What methods are used for a hysterectomy?"}, {"id": "S029", "text": "A hysterectomy may be done several different ways."}, {"id": "S030", "text": "Your provider will determine the best method for the surgery based on your general health, the reason for the surgery, and other factors."}, {"id": "S031", "text": "Methods to perform a hysterectomy include: Abdominal hysterectomy."}, {"id": "S032", "text": "A cut is made in your lower abdomen (belly)."}, {"id": "S033", "text": "Your provider may recommend this method if you have a large uterus or to check other pelvic organs for signs of disease."}, {"id": "S034", "text": "This surgery has a longer recovery time than the others."}, {"id": "S035", "text": "This may not be an option if you have very large fibroids."}, {"id": "S036", "text": "Uses an instrument with a thin, lighted tube and an attached camera."}, {"id": "S037", "text": "This helps your provider see your pelvic organs."}, {"id": "S038", "text": "Small cuts are made in either your abdomen (belly) or vagina."}, {"id": "S039", "text": "This is not an option for all types of uterine fibroids."}, {"id": "S040", "text": "Your provider guides a robotic arm to do the surgery through small cuts in your lower abdomen (belly)."}, {"id": "S041", "text": "After a hysterectomy , it can take four to six weeks to recover, depending on the type of surgery you have."}, {"id": "S042", "text": "Like all surgeries, a hysterectomy has risks, even though the results are usually good."}, {"id": "S043", "text": "Talk to your provider about the benefits and risks of having a hysterectomy."}, {"id": "S044", "text": "More serious risks can include: Too much bleeding during surgery Infection Blood clots Dept."}, {"id": "S045", "text": "of Health and Human Services Office on Women's Health"}]}, {"id": "MLP-3698", "title": "Rural Health Concerns", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Around 15% of people in the United States live in rural areas."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "There are many different reasons why you might choose to live in a rural community."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "You may want a lower cost of living and a slower pace of life."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "You may enjoy having access to big, open spaces for recreation."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Rural areas are less crowded and can offer more privacy."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "You may choose a rural area so that you can live near your family and friends."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "But there are also challenges to living in a rural area, including when it comes to taking care of your health."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Compared to urban areas, rural communities tend to have: Higher poverty rates."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "A higher percentage of older adults, who are more likely to have chronic health problems."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "More residents without health insurance."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "For example, clinics and hospitals may be far away."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "Higher rates of certain substance use, such as cigarette smoking and opioid and methamphetamine misuse."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "Higher rates of chronic health problems such as high blood pressure and obesity ."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "More exposure to environmental hazards, such as chemicals used for farming."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "There are solutions to deal with these problems."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "A few examples include: Clinics offering telehealth to provide care for people who live far away from specialists or can't easily get to their providers' offices."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "Local public health agencies working with their communities to promote healthy living."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "They can provide wellness and exercise classes and start a farmer's market."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "Local governments adding bike lanes and trails to encourage people to bike and walk."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "Rural schools can offer counseling and mental health services for their students."}]}]
